t: The regime grew out of the Nationalist side of the Spanish Civil War: Franco was recognised as Caudillo on 1 October 1936 and in April 1937 merged the Falange and the Carlists into the FET y de las JONS, the sole legal party.

Victory in 1939 was followed by mass imprisonment, executions and exile; by the regime's own figures more than 270,000 people were held in prisons and some 500,000 had fled, and more than 200,000 Spaniards are estimated to have died from 1940 to 1942 of persecution, hunger and disease.

After isolation and autarky, the liberalisation of 1959 opened the "Spanish Miracle" of the 1960s, but political parties and independent unions stayed banned until Franco's death on 20 November 1975 opened the transition to democracy.
dyk: Under the Law of Political Responsibility of February 1939, parishes were granted policing powers equal to those of local officials and Falange leaders, and some official jobs required a statement of "good behaviour" from a priest.
ev: The Junta de Defensa Nacional, governing the Nationalist-held territories, recognises Franco as Caudillo of Spain on 1 October
In April Franco merges the Falange Española de las JONS with the Carlist Comunión Tradicionalista to form the Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las JONS
The Nationalists win the Spanish Civil War, and the Falange is declared the sole legally sanctioned party
Franco and Hitler meet at Hendaye on 23 October, but the talks on Spain's entry into the Second World War end in failure
Spain is declared a kingdom on 26 July, with Franco as regent for life and the sole right to appoint his successor
Under pressure from the United States, the IMF and the technocrats of Opus Dei, the regime liberalises the economy
Franco designates Juan Carlos of Bourbon as his heir, and Spain closes its border with Gibraltar
Franco dies on 20 November, and Juan Carlos becomes King of Spain

f.founder: Francisco Franco, recognised as Caudillo of Spain by the Junta de Defensa Nacional on 1 October 1936
f.predecessor: Second Spanish Republic; in the Nationalist zone, the Junta de Defensa Nacional
f.successor: Kingdom of Spain under Juan Carlos, through the Spanish transition to democracy
